name: Agentic Research Orchestrator
tag: Five research agents split up a computer-science question, read the sources and report back with citations.

scenarios.title: Pick a vector database
scenarios.ask: Compare vector databases for {vectors} million embeddings with a {latency} ms query budget. Read at least {papers} sources.
steps: Planner
Split the question into 5 parts: index types, scale limits, latency, cost and operations.
Literature agent
Read {papers} sources: benchmark write-ups, docs and papers on HNSW and IVF indexes.
Benchmark agent
Pulled published results near {vectors} million vectors and noted test hardware for each.
Skeptic agent
Flagged {=max(1, round(papers * 0.15))} sources with vendor-run benchmarks and weighted them lower.
Writer
Merged findings into a short report with a citation on every claim.

result.title: Research report
rows: {=min(4, max(2, round(latency / 40) + 1))} options under {latency} ms in published tests
Run your own test on a sample

followups: Only partly. Hardware, settings and data shape differ. The report lists the setup for each number so you can judge, and the Skeptic agent marks vendor-run results.
How was the memory number calculated?
Each 768-dimension vector in 32-bit floats takes 3,072 bytes, so {vectors} million vectors need about {=round(vectors * 3.072, 1)} GB before the index adds its own overhead.

scenarios.title: Literature review for a proposal
scenarios.ask: Summarize the last {years} years of research on {topic} for a grant proposal.
steps: Planner
Defined search terms and split the {years}-year window across the agents.
Search agent
Found about {=years * topic * 40} candidate papers and kept {=round(years * topic * 40 * 0.15)} after abstract screening.
Reader agents
Extracted method, dataset and main result from each kept paper.
Gap finder
Grouped papers into themes and listed {=2 + topic} open problems that few papers address.
Writer
Drafted a two-page related-work section with references.
followups: Every reference links to a source the agents actually retrieved. The Writer cannot cite anything that is not in the reading list, and you can open each one.
Can I add papers I already know?
Yes. Drop in a list of titles or PDFs and they are read first and marked as seeded by you.

scenarios.title: Explain a production bug
scenarios.ask: Our cache shows stale reads under load in {regions} regions. Research known causes and fixes.
steps: Planner
Framed it as a consistency question: replication lag, invalidation order or clock issues.
Literature agent
Read design notes and papers on cache invalidation and read-your-writes consistency.
Incident agent
Found {=4 + regions} public postmortems with similar symptoms.
Skeptic agent
Ruled out clock skew because the stale reads cluster on writes followed by reads within 50 ms.
Writer
Ranked 3 likely causes with a test to confirm each.

result.title: Findings
rows: Stale reads per day at 1B reads

followups: Can it look at our logs?
If you connect them, yes. A sixth agent can check the timing pattern in your logs against each likely cause.
It is a starting point, not a diagnosis. Each cause comes with a test so your team can confirm or rule it out quickly.
